mission: Forensically examine the 6 anchor-free phase abstentions remaining after E04 (v2.3, 12/18) and convert to answers ONLY where evidence genuinely supports it, as a versioned v2.4 contract.

datasetScope.goldCases: the 18 committed wave-a gold phase cases used by E04 / d3-05 (datasets/experiments/wave-d3/d3-05-measure-gold.ts); grouped by source clip (faead, 944403, wgm-wheelchair, sasebo, marne, dense-dink), never random-frame splits
datasetScope.heldOut: wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 untouched (not viewed, labeled, tuned against, or regenerated)

contractChange.rule: Measurement-resolution apex adoption: the strongest margin sample above the in-event peak that is motion-connected to it may be adopted as this event's apex ONLY when every motion-connected margin sample above the in-event peak lies within one median inter-sample gap of the event boundary. Event labels are quantized to frames and speeds are sampled at finite intervals, so an apex one sample past the boundary is indistinguishable from an in-event apex at measurement resolution. A connected excess extending farther out is a real spillover and still abstains (PHASE_PEAK_OUTSIDE_EVENT); rest-separated margin motion is never adopted (still a neighboring stroke). No thresholds, floors, sample-count minima, or denominators were weakened; the in-event 0.5 speed floor is applied BEFORE adoption, so weak in-event evidence cannot be rescued by a margin peak. Anchored path untouched.

sixCases.forensicFinding: Strong in-event peak (1.06 at 14333ms); the true apex (1.29 at 14348ms) sits 15ms past the event end with a 15-16ms median sample interval, motion-connected (valley 0.82 of in-event peak), prominence 3.04x padded median, no other sample above the in-event peak, no rivals of the adopted apex.
sixCases.decision: CONVERTED (v2.4): apex within one sampling interval of the boundary and motion-connected — indistinguishable from an in-event apex at measurement resolution.
sixCases.v24Outcome: segmented (motionPeakMs 14348, ordered, invariant-clean after JSON round-trip)

sixCases.forensicFinding: In-event peak 0.454 below the floor; padded max 1.3 sits 84ms (>2 sample intervals of 41.7ms) outside and is rest-separated from the in-event motion (valley 0.009) — it is a neighboring stroke, not this event's apex.
sixCases.decision: KEPT ABSTAINED: converting would require weakening the 0.5 in-event floor or adopting a rest-separated neighboring stroke's apex.

sixCases.forensicFinding: No meaningful swing anywhere: in-event peak 0.171, padded max 0.178 (245ms outside, rest-separated, with a near-equal rival). Anchored path also reports no meaningful swing speed in the window.
sixCases.decision: KEPT ABSTAINED: no motion evidence exists to segment.

sixCases.forensicFinding: Periodic multi-burst motion: in-event rival 4.25 at 182933ms vs apex 4.35 at 182467ms (within 10%), plus a stronger margin sample 8.04. In-event rivals always contest — there is no single swing apex.
sixCases.decision: KEPT ABSTAINED: honest ambiguity; regression-pinned in phaseRedTeam (D3-05 B2).

sixCases.forensicFinding: In-event peak 0.323 below the floor; the connected margin sample 0.362 (19ms outside) is also below the floor. The floor is applied before adoption, so adoption cannot rescue this case — and should not: total motion is too weak to be a swing.
sixCases.decision: KEPT ABSTAINED: weak evidence throughout; converting would weaken the floor.

sixCases.forensicFinding: In-event peak 0.239 below the floor; the stronger margin peak 0.676 (48ms outside) is rest-separated (valley 0.013) — a neighboring stroke. The anchored path segments this case using the gold contact; anchor-free evidence alone is insufficient.
sixCases.decision: KEPT ABSTAINED: adopting a rest-separated neighboring stroke's apex would be relabeling motion, not evidence.
